title: CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens could force Cowboys into franchise-altering  choice
description: The Cowboys have one of the NFL’s most dangerous receiving duos in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but Stephen Jones admits keeping both stars could create a massive financial challenge.
fullText:
CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens could force Cowboys into franchise-altering choice originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Dallas Cowboys have constructed one of the NFL's most dangerous receiving tandems. Keeping it together beyond 2026 could prove much more difficult.

CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens give quarterback Dak Prescott two legitimate No. 1 options, but executive vice president Stephen Jones acknowledged Dallas could eventually face a difficult financial decision.

"I don't know of any teams that really can pay two top receivers top of the market," Jones said on the DLLS Cowboys podcast. "So that's gonna be a real difficult situation as we move forward."

For now, Dallas has pushed that conversation into 2027.

Pickens is playing the 2026 season on the $27.298 million franchise tag after producing 1,429 receiving yards and nine touchdowns last season. Rather than immediately committing to another massive contract, the Cowboys want the 25-year-old to put together consecutive productive seasons.

Pickens, meanwhile, has seemingly embraced the opportunity.

"George is really wanting to put back-to-back years on top of one another so it'll help his market," Jones said.

That's where Dallas' potential problem begins.

Lamb already carries one of the NFL's richest receiver contracts, averaging $34 million with three years remaining. If Pickens delivers another elite season, his asking price could climb into similar territory.

Teams have successfully invested heavily in two receivers. Cincinnati has done so with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, though carrying two premium contracts at the position requires significant salary-cap maneuvering.

Dallas isn't worrying about that yet.

The Cowboys instead appear focused on maximizing their current championship window. Prescott has Lamb and Pickens on the outside, tight end Jake Ferguson provides another established target, and Ryan Flournoy gives Dallas additional depth.

The combination could create matchup problems throughout the NFC.

But every big Pickens performance this season could simultaneously increase the price of keeping him.

Dallas wanted another year of evidence before making a long-term commitment.

If Pickens delivers it, the Cowboys could enter next offseason facing exactly the kind of expensive decision Jones already knows is coming.

fullText:
From Day 1 of training camp, the Dallas Cowboys looked like a completely different team.

The Cowboys had strong practices and were competitive against the Los Angeles Rams in their joint practice. In the preseason, they finished 2-1, with double-digit wins over the Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals.

After a successful five weeks of training camp and preseason games, the Cowboys appear to be one of the biggest winners so far in the NFL. They got that vindication with a single grade.

CBS Sports writer Tyler Sullivan gave every NFL team grades on how they did in 2026. Sullivan gave the Cowboys a B+.

"Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and a number of other key Cowboys starters didn't partake in the preseason. That said, there was plenty of intrigue on the offensive side of the ball as Sam Howell and Joe Milton duked it out for the backup role. Howell won out, with Milton being waived. On defense, third-round linebacker Jaishawn Barham opened eyes with his play this summer, giving Dallas some much-needed depth at the position with upside for more. Undrafted wideout Camden Brown made the opening 53-man roster after catching six balls for 166 yards and two touchdowns this preseason. Meanwhile, from a player-acquisition standpoint, the Cowboys added pass rusher Von Miller and offensive tackle Broderick Jones during the preseason. Again, the headliners that we'll see in Week 1 stayed behind the scenes, but Dallas put together a solid summer."

Dallas' offense led the charge with great passing performances from Milton and Howell, who both had over 300 yards each in three games. Even on defense, the Cowboys allowed just 20 points in their first two games against the Seahawks and Cardinals.

This team is improved in every aspect on offense, defense, and special teams. After going 7-9-1 last season, the Cowboys have the makings of a playoff team in 2026.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer is now in Year 2 on the job and has Christian Parker running the defense. Dallas added a ton of talent, including Von Miller and Broderick Jones, to further improve the roster in the preseason.

They still have a lot of work to do, but this franchise is finally heading in the right direction. After missing the playoffs two years in a row, it feels more realistic that they can compete for not only a playoff spot, but for the NFC East title.

A roster this deep is what the Cowboys needed to turn things around. This team is trending in the right direction.

title: Remember these clips if the Dallas Cowboys stink
description: It's once again that time of year when Cowboys hype rockets out of control.
fullText:
It's a day that ends in "y" so that means the Dallas Cowboys are all over the sports talk shows. Brian Schottenheimer's side will be featured on Sunday Night Football for a Week 1 matchup against the hated New York Giants and we'll finally have some meaningful football to fuel reactions. But until things kick off, the only thing to do is to look ahead and make bold claims.

Both Jordan Rodgers and Adam Schefter took advantage of the opportunity on Wednesday's Get Up.

"On paper, this defense can get them to the Super Bowl because of how good the offense is," Rodgers surmised. "This defense needs to go from one of the worst to just good, middle of the pack."

Schefter agreed, channeling his rosy outlook for the Cowboys into the most important thing—how it impacts Stephen A. Smith.

"I got some bad news for Stephen A. Smith," Schefter said. "The Dallas Cowboys are coming!"

It feels like an annual tradition to hype up the Cowboys before they inevitably have a disappointing season. We've been doing it for three decades now with precious little evidence showing that it ever works.

No doubt, some of you want it to stop. Considering the team's accomplishments in comparison to some other franchises this century, there is absolutely no reason for them to dominate as much of the spotlight as they do. Yet I am going to offer a bit of a rebuttal steeped in cynicism.

The America's Team thing worked. There's a reason why Dallas finds itself in the A or B block even when they don't warranted it. Heck, even when there's nothing of substance to really discuss. It's not that they have to shove the Cowboys down our throats all the time but they also have to do what's best to stand out in an attention economy.

MORE: Previewing all 16 NFC teams & predicting every record in 2026

People who are tired by the song and dance can take solace in knowing that there are always a blessing of wonderful clips that don't age well whenever the Cowboys fall on their face. So if history is any guide, a little patience is required for a snarky payout down the line.

Or, if you are a believer in Dallas, bookmark this page and dance all over my grave if the Cowboys do, in fact, win it all.

title: Former Cowboys QB Tony Romo pleads no contest to OWI, addresses alcohol struggles
description: Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo pleaded no contest to OWI following his July arrest in Milwaukee and addressed his struggles with alcohol.
fullText:
Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo pleaded no contest Tuesday to operating while intoxicated in connection with his July arrest in Milwaukee, according to WISN 12.

Romo, 46, will have his driver's license revoked for six months and must pay a $784 fine. He also must complete an alcohol assessment program and install an ignition interlock device on any vehicle he owns.

Milwaukee County sheriff's deputies arrested Romo, a Wisconsin native, on July 23 after a traffic stop.

According to a search warrant obtained by WISN 12, a deputy reported smelling a "strong odor of an alcoholic beverage" on Romo's breath. Body-camera footage showed Romo telling the deputy he had not consumed any alcohol.

ALSO READ: Dear Dallas Cowboys, please make the Super Bowl again before I die

Citations obtained by WISN 12 state that deputies found an open bottle of an alcoholic beverage on the passenger side of Romo's vehicle. Court records also show he was cited for refusing an intoxication test and first-offense operating while intoxicated.

In Wisconsin, a first-offense OWI is generally treated as a civil traffic violation rather than a criminal offense.

Romo addressed the case in an Instagram statement Tuesday, saying he took responsibility for his actions.

"This morning, I faced a recent personal failure by pleading no contest to a civil offense for OWI in Wisconsin," Romo said. "I own this completely."

Romo said multiple back surgeries following his NFL career left him with persistent pain and led to a dependence on pain medication. His efforts to stop using the medication eventually contributed to an over-reliance on alcohol, he said, while emphasizing that it did not excuse his actions.

Romo is currently on leave from CBS Sports, where he is part of the network's lead NFL broadcast team. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that former Wisconsin Badgers and NFL star J.J. Watt will fill in during Romo's absence.

Romo spent his entire 14-year NFL career with the Cowboys, earning four Pro Bowl selections before retiring after the 2016 season and joining CBS.

There's more to San Antonio with the Express-News.

title: Cowboys want Joe Milton back on the practice squad
description: In a bit of a surprise move, the Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton on Monday.
fullText:
In a bit of a surprise move, the Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton on Monday. They hope to sign him back to the practice squad.

Dallas named Sam Howell the backup to Dak Prescott and left Milton temporarily out of work after the Cowboys claimed running back Emari Demercado and needed a roster spot.

Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer and executive vice president Stephen Jones both said Tuesday that they want Milton back on the practice squad as the team's third quarterback. Milton's departure would necessitate signing a different third quarterback.

The Cowboys are waiting to see if Milton clears waivers.

"Joe obviously played really good in the preseason games," Jones said on All DLLS Cowboys. "We really liked his performance. Sam did as well. But at the end of the day, when you took the full body of work in training camp, the practices against other teams, the coaches thought — albeit really close — Sam was the best choice for the team to go with as two now. We'd love to have Joe back. A lot of teams in this league figure out ways to carry three and four [quarterbacks]. We've got a lot of stress on our roster with this new defense and things that we're doing that we can carry two [quarterbacks]. We're in talks with Joe. We'll see if he gets claimed. If he doesn't, we'd love to have Joe back as our three and on the practice squad."

In three preseason games, Milton completed 29 of 43 passes for 378 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. He added 12 carries for 14 yards and a rushing touchdown.

The Cowboys traded a fifth-round pick to New England for Milton in the 2025 offseason, and he served as Prescott's backup last season.

title: Ex-Cowboys QB Predicted To Become “Final Nail In Shedeur Sanders’ Time With Browns”: Analyst

fullText:
Since former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Joe Milton III is now available, the Cleveland Browns might be interested in signing him. This may not be good news for Shedeur Sanders if Browns reporter Jared Mueller is to be believed.

Bringing in Milton will likely mean that either Sanders, Dillon Gabriel or the rookie, Taylen Green, will have to leave, because having five quarterbacks is a non-brainer. Even four quarterbacks, which the Browns currently have on their roster, is too much.

Since Milton has experience and Green is a rookie, Sanders is the most likely player to be let go if Milton is signed as per Mueller.

"Whatever you think about Sanders' talent, last year he lost a quarterback competition to the aged Joe Flacco and the undersized Gabriel," Mueller writes. "All three played poorly in 2025. Then, this year with a new coaching staff and added talent around him, Sanders lost a quarterback competition to Deshaun Watson, who hasn't been good for half a decade and is coming off missing a year and a half of football. None of that screams that the Cleveland organization is high on Sanders."

"Claiming Milton could just be the final nail in Sanders' time with the Browns," Mueller added.

If the Browns decide to replace Sanders with Milton, general manager Andrew Berry might trade Sanders to a team looking for a young QB with high potential. However, this year, even with new coaches and better teammates, Sanders lost the QB1 competition to veteran Watson.

Watson said on Monday that he did not know he would start until coach Monken told him that morning.

"This is what I've been working for for two years, to show that I'm capable of being the starter for one of the 32 organizations in this league," Watson said. "It felt good and a lot of excitement, but it comes with a lot of work, too."

Monken said that the Browns do not plan to change their starting QB from week to week.

"I think Shedeur has done a great job, come a long ways, and we're excited about his future," Monken added, "but this is not a week-to-week decision."

Instead of getting upset, Sanders took the high road and spoke out against the fans who booed Watson in the preseason game vs. the Buffalo Bills.

"I don't appreciate that at all," Sanders said. "Just, regardless of competition, we all human beings, and I think we all need to understand that."

"Just for all the fans and everything, I really appreciate ya'll showing up and everything," he added. "And however ya'll feel about the situation, about with Deshaun, about with everything, still I think it's about bigger purpose of just respect."

The Browns will play their Week 1 game on Sunday, September 13, against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium.

title: Tony Romo faces three new citations from last month's OWI arrest in Milwaukee
description: More than a month after former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo was arrested for suspicion of operating while intoxicated in Milwaukee, the authorities have filed three new citations against him.
fullText:
More than a month after former Cowboys quarterback and CBS broadcaster Tony Romo was arrested for suspicion of operating while intoxicated in Milwaukee, the authorities have filed three new citations against him.

Via TMZ, the district attorney has charged Romo with first-offense operating while intoxicated, unsafe passing on the right side, and possessing open intoxicants in his vehicle.

Romo was placed on leave by CBS eight days after the arrest, which created multiple bodycam videos that created a general bad look for Romo. CBS has elevated J.J. Watt to replace Romo on the network's top broadcast team, and it seems to be a move that will cover the entire season.

Romo has four years left on his CBS contract, at a total payout of $72 million. CBS could try to terminate the deal for cause, owing him nothing. Romo would surely fight such a move. A settlement for something less than the full amount is always possible.

title: Detroit Lions sign former Cowboys, Chiefs CB ahead of preseason finale
description: Ahead of its preseason finale, the Detroit Lions signed former Dallas Cowboys and Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Eric Scott Jr.
fullText:
Ahead of its preseason finale and then roster cuts, the Detroit Lions inked former Dallas Cowboys and Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Eric Scott Jr. to its 90-man roster. Scott is a 6-foot, 197-pound corner.

Scott was drafted by the Cowboys in the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. While he's yet to make his NFL debut, Scott may get the chance to impress and put some tape together in the Lions' final preseason game on Saturday at the Indianapolis Colts.

Whether it's with Detroit or another NFL franchise, a strong showing on Saturday against the Colts would set Scott up to potentially make a 53-man roster or an NFL practice squad.

Lions have placed EDGE Payton Turner on Reserve/Injured and signed DB Eric Scott. pic.twitter.com/pq9Pzy4kKg

Inactive throughout his 2023 rookie year, Scott was waived by Dallas near the end of training camp, then claimed by Kansas City, where he joined the Chiefs' 2024 practice squad. Unfortunately for Scott, he suffered an injury that forced him to the injured reserve near the end of training camp and cost him the entire 2025 season with the Chiefs.

Scott made the Cowboys roster entering his rookie season, but he never saw the field and was declared inactive each game. In 2024, the Cowboys waived Scott near the end of training camp. The Chiefs claimed Scott off waivers and he ended up on Kansas City's practice squad in 2024.

Then, an undisclosed injury forced Scott to the Chiefs' injured reserve in 2025.

Scott began his college career at Illinois State, transferred to Butler Community College, and finished at Southern Mississippi. Scott totaled four interceptions and 11 passes defended while at Southern Mississippi.

In its corresponding move, the Lions placed EDGE Payton Turner on injured reserve, ending his 2026 season before it ever began.

Kickoff between the Lions and Colts on Saturday is set for 1 p.m. ET on the NFL Network.

title: George Pickens and the Top 10 Cowboys playing in contract year in 2026
description: Contract years tend to bring out the best in players, as long as the team is in contention. Here's a look at the top Cowboys with a lot to play for.
fullText:
At the end of the day, this is a business. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones will never let anyone forget that plain fact, though he does bank on fanaticism blurring the lines in his favor far too often. Star NFL players have a passion for the game that allows them to put their bodies through the rigors of untold physical hardships. Often times the willingness to push their bodies 100% is the difference between being talented and being great.

But at the end of the day, the reward of millions of dollars is certainly a motivating factor. Each NFL player contributes to an NFL machine that creates billions in revenue, and rightly they want their fair share. With a collective bargaining agreement and a salary cap, the parameters are put in place for how much a player can earn, and their contracts determine when they are eligible to earn the most.

So contract years, the final season on a player's current deal, mean a ton. Players are either looking to convince heir current clubs to offer extensions, or they are auditioning for one of the other 31 clubs in free agency. That's the case for between 15-20 players on each team every season, and this year the Cowboys contingent is headlined by WR George Pickens.

Here's a look at the top Cowboys who are playing for their next big payday.

Anger is 38 and entering his 15th season. He hasn't been All-Pro worthy in a couple seasons, but he's more than serviceable and could extend his career in Dallas or elsewhere in 2027.

Miller is ring chasing at this point, but who knows how long the 37-year old will try to keep playing. A series of late-camp invites seem to be in his future as long as he can be a rotational contributor good for five sacks or more each season.

Patience is a virtue, and though he may still be WR6 for Dallas entering the season, Mingo has certainly turned the corner entering his fourth year in the league. That's if training camp and preseason are actually precursors. Mingo's biggest issue is that he may be bona fide, but may never see the field unless catastrophe strikes the league's top WR group.

Houston had 5.5 sacks last year and could be part of a much improved team effort in taking down the quarterback. Edge rushers get paid, even rotational ones, and having back-to-back years of health and production could be huge for his lifetime earnings.

Winters was a reserve he played a lot in SF after Fred Warner's injuries, but the 49ers traded him away. If he takes on a starter's role, mentality and leadership in his first season in Dallas, he certainly could earn an extension or a strong look on the open market come March.

Hooker took a pay cut to remain in Dallas, but Dallas didn't want to release him outright. Both speak volumes. Even if the Cowboys are done with him as a starter (now or after the year), he's rehabilitated his image as an injured player and should be able to latch on elsewhere in 2027.

Flournoy is a restricted free agent, but if he reaches the lofty goal of a 1,000-yard receiving season as the Cowboys' WR3, he'll earn a second-round tender at a minimum, if not a first. And that still might have other teams calling to submit an offer sheet.

Dallas seems to have high hopes on Durant elevating his play from what he was with the Rams now that he's in Christian Parker's system. If that comes to fruition, he could earn a solid contract in free agency this offseason.

Bass has a chance to not start a single game and still get paid; that's how good he's been in spot duty over the years, leading to being a second-round tender RFA this season. He can start for at least a dozen teams in the NFL right now.

Overshown's first mission is proving he can play an entire season's worth of games, something he hasn't done in three professional years. If he can do that, then his talent will take care of the rest as he's one of the most athletic linebackers in the league.

Pickens' situation is unique, as he's playing on the franchise tag and more than likely will be tagged again when the new league year comes around. He's absolutely auditioning for a long-term deal, whether in Dallas or in another city. He'll try to convince 31 other teams he's so good that he deserves top-of-the-market money AND trade compensation the Cowboys will rightfully demand if they don't extend him themselves.

title: Cowboys have done something for first time since 2007
description: The Cowboys have done something for the first time since 2007
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys are 2-0 in the preseason. Alert the masses.

Before we go any further, we all agree that wins and losses in the preseason do not ultimately matter. You would certainly rather win these exhibition contests than lose them, but at the end of the day that particular detail does not matter as much as the roster growth and development you ideally experience within them.

That being said, it has had been almost 20 years since the Cowboys could say that they were 2-0 in a given preseason. As we discussed this past week the last season where this was the case was 2007.

Many around here believe that 2007 was the best team that the Cowboys have fielded throughout the entirety of The Drought™ so perhaps this is an indication that 2026 will be as successful as that one was, ideally without the exact same finish. Obviously we are just having fun with all of this, but it is pretty wild that the Cowboys had gone so long without getting to 2-0 in the preseason, isn't it?

Consider that the Cowboys got to 1-0 in the preseason last week for the first time since 2017. This offseason, and now preseason have felt so much like the Cowboys doing things they haven't done in a long time, and that trend is certainly continuing.

title: Arizona Cardinals struggle in preseason loss to Dallas Cowboys

fullText:

title: Cowboys Preseason Stock Up: That's James Houston leading the way
description: In a terrific defensive performance, the Dallas Cowboys saw James Houston, Reddy Steward, and Julius Wood step up and play well in preseason game one.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys started their game against the Seattle Seahawks allowing a 13-play drive for 80 yards that lasted over seven minutes. It felt like watching the 2025 defense, but from then on they didn't allow a single point, forced two three-and-outs, and conjured up a goal-line stand on a four-and-out to seal the victory.

The defense was terrific overall, going from 19 missed tackles in last season's first preseason game to zero against Seattle.

They held the Seahawks offense to 14 first downs, only two yards per pass, under four yards per rush attempt, and one touchdown in four red-zone trips. Seattle managed only 29 passing yards after the opening drive and went under 50% on third- and fourth-down conversions. The incredible play leaves plenty of options for players to see their stock rise on the Dallas defense, but here are the top three.

The post-game signing of Von Miller makes every snap more important for every edge not named Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezieruaku, and Malachi Lawrence. James Houston could be in a battle for one spot with Sam Williams, Tyrus Wheat, Isaiah Land, and Marist Liufau, and he stepped up against the Seahawks once again.

He had three tackles, a sack, a tackle for a loss, and a QB hit. Houston was the highest-rated defensive player by Pro Football Focus (PFF) with an 86.5 overall grade. He was already a tough cut after how he produced last season, but his first game of 2026 was another step to the 53-man roster.

Reddy Steward wasn't gifted with the frame of a cornerback the Cowboys typically search for. He is under 6 feet and only 180 pounds, but his grit and determination led him to play in all 17 games last season, including five starts. The new regime had most fans believing he was on his way out, but this game might be turning the tide in his favor.

He makes plays, stays around the ball, and isn't afraid to make a tackle or break up a pass. Steward ended the game with three tackles, half a sack, and a QB hit as possibly the best corner for Dallas in the game.

Julius Wood is beginning to look like a sure thing to make this team at a position that already includes Jalen Thompson, Caleb Downs, Malik Hooker, and P.J. Locke. He is a drumbeat player in camp, like Camden Brown, noticed in every practice on defense and special teams. Now he's making an impact in real game situations.

He was second on the team in tackles and had the third-highest PFF grade. Wood is different because, beyond the stats, the plays he makes are impactful. The hits are felt at a level higher than others on the defense. His tackle at the goal line isn't one every player could make in this secondary, and it led to a goal-line stand to close out the game.

Jerry Jones and the Dallas Cowboys enter the 2026 NFL season with hopes of getting back to the playoffs and being a Super Bowl contender.

Throughout the course of the offseason, the Cowboys were heavily rumored to make a big splash addition. That opportunity never ended up materializing for Dallas.

Among the most notable offseason moves were the trade for pass rusher Rashan Gary, trading up in the NFL Draft to get Caleb Downs, and the decision to franchise tag wide receiver George Pickens instead of giving him a contract extension. In recent years, Dallas has continually come up short of expectations. Jones has been very vocal about being willing to do whatever it takes to get the Cowboys back to the Super Bowl.

With that being said, a former NFL star and Super Bowl winner has spoken out with a strong shot directed at the Dallas franchise owner.

Mark Schlereth, a Denver Broncos' legend, recently took a shot at Jones on social media. The shot came after a question from a fan.

"Mark! Do you think it's Jerry's ego or ignorance that is holding the cowboys back?" the fan questioned.

"All the above," Schlereth wrote.

As previously mentioned, Jones has been very vocal about his desire to be a championship contender. Should Dallas come up short of those expectations, changes could be made.

Throughout his tenure as the Cowboys' owner, Jones hasn't always been patient. He wants to win and coming up short of that can trigger a quick decision.

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer is entering his second season as the head coach in Dallas. He has received strong praise from Jones, but missing the playoffs in 2026 could bring a coaching change. title: Seahawks Studs & Duds in preseason Week 1 loss to Cowboys
description: With 3:45 to go, Jalan Gaines was nodding along, sweat pouring off, getting coached by Derick Hall mid-water break. Standout edge player of the night.
fullText:
The Seattle Seahawks lost 17-7 to the Dallas Cowboys, and we've recapped the game here and talked about the top takeaways here, but the most exciting part of the night is when we get to discuss the individual players who made a case to move up in roster status. We'll get into six of the biggest standout performances- both good and bad- here, while we'll save some of the others for deep dives this week.

Here is your preseason Week 1 edition of Studs & Duds, your first of many for the 2026 NFL Season. I went with five varied studs and one big position group of duds, which accurately represented how this game felt to watch.

Montorie Foster Jr. has a formidable frame for a possession wide receiver, so it made sense why the Seahawks signed him last year as soon as you saw a picture. The more ripped receivers of this ilk usually work well on special teams, too. Tonight, though, he caught 5 of 7 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown, leading the team in all four categories. The team's lone score was cool and a good play, sure; but he won't be asked to do that in the regular season. He can follow a similar path to the roster than the one Dareke Young took- earning trust as a backup and special teamer above all other candidates with prerequisite size. He ticks those boxes.

You can't see it on the stat sheet, but Mason Richman played a ton in this game, and brought an impressive level of intensity on nearly every play he did. He might have been the best player on the first and only scoring drive, in which the run game started strong, with him as the key pulling guard on several instances. His athleticism seems better than the No. 234 pick he was selected with would suggest, and his pre-draft testing showed some clear strengths and weaknesses; but for a backup guard, he looked as good as any the Seahawks have had in recent memory.

Tyrice Knight has been looking excellent in drills, and he was one of the best players on the field in the first half. He led the entire game with ten tackles (seven solo) and two passes defended. He has an incredible motor that can make for impact plays, but has struggled with consistency play-to-play, with occasional lapses evening the high points out. To see him fill up and dominate the stat sheet is as encouraging a sign as any in this game. Defending so well against both the run and pass game at once, though? That's how players force their way onto the field in Mike Macdonald's defense.

Rylie Mills had to be double-teamed almost immediately, and is starting to look like he's just a higher level player than his draft stock originally suggested. The Seahawks were lucky to get him with the No. 142 pick. Most teams aren't having a player who got a sack in the Super Bowl six months ago play in the preseason opener, but Mills is a rare case. He also gets to sit behind Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy II, the former of whom was interviewed on the local KIRO 7 broadcast and said Mills "reminded him of himself." Don't overreact, but that's not the type of praise most second-year defensive tackles get.

Gallons of sweat pouring off, 3:45 to go in the fourth quarter, and Jalan Gaines is nodding along, getting coached by Derick Hall mid-water break. Gaines was the standout edge player of the night, who visibly improved over the course of the night as much as anyone. The effort was unquestionable after a close-up of his jersey showed the sweat equity, and his technique kept winning against Dallas' tackles. He deserves to be talked about as an outside roster candidate until further notice in a position of relative need.

I wasn't impressed by the plethora of depth cornerbacks the Seahawks have brought in this offseason. I feel bad for Shemar Jean-Charles, giving Camden Brown an inside release and ending up on the wrong side of a 39-yard highlight reel touchdown, even getting beat at multiple points on the rep. It might not be as bad as that one play looked for him, but I didn't think the others had great days either. Andre Fuller is explosive vertically, in a straight line, and is big, but his hips worry me in the nickel spot. I thought Joe Milton worked the crossing routes against him easier than he should've. Michael Dansby allowed Camden Brown's second highlight-reel touchdown, this time a one-handed acrobatic goal-line fade. It also looked worse than it probably was, but doesn't bode well for him competing with the others. I didn't notice Noah Igbinoghene or Nehemiah Pritchett much, so they'd both be ahead of those three right now, and hopefully Julian Neal has an easier time adapting. Luckily, Terrion Arnold could plug this hole relatively quickly once he begins practicing.

title: Grantsville rallies from 12-point deficit, scores 30 unanswered to stun San Juan 30-20
description: For the first quarter and a half against Grantsville Friday, it looked like San Juan was going to remind everyone why it was one of the most dangerous offensive teams in Utah.  Then Grantsville’s defense took over.  The Cowboys erased a 12-0 deficit by scoring 30 unanswered points, forcing seven San Juan turnovers along the way, and held on for a 30-20 victory at Snow College.
fullText:
For the first quarter and a half against Grantsville Friday, it looked like San Juan was going to remind everyone why it was one of the most dangerous offensive teams in Utah.

Then Grantsville's defense took over.

The Cowboys erased a 12-0 deficit by scoring 30 unanswered points, forcing seven San Juan turnovers along the way, and held on for a 30-20 victory at Snow College.

It was a game that seemed to change every few minutes. San Juan came out firing as quarterback Beau Yeomans opened the scoring with a 1-yard touchdown run, and later in the first quarter he found Brigg Palmer wide open for a 47-yard touchdown.

Just like that, San Juan had a 12-0 lead.

And then the Broncos stopped scoring, although it took a while for the Cowboys offense to get going as they threw two interceptions deep in San Juan territory.

But Grantsville's defense kept giving the offense another chance.

"We left a lot of points on the board," Grantsville coach David Millward said. "We had interceptions in the end zone. I think we had four red-zone possessions without points."

Eventually, though, the Cowboys broke through when Carter Bell scored on a 9-yard run early in the second quarter, cutting San Juan's lead to 12-7.

Then late in the first half, Mack Hammond intercepted Yeomans and gave Grantsville the ball at its own 42. Crew Allred immediately ripped off a 34-yard run, and then with 2.4 seconds left before halftime, Allred rolled to his left and found Ty Holm for a 24-yard touchdown.

Suddenly, the team that had trailed 12-0 was leading 13-12.

The Cowboys opened the second half by forcing another San Juan turnover when Palmer fumbled at the San Juan 30.

Grantsville turned that opportunity into another touchdown, with Bell punching it in from the goal line. A successful two-point conversion pushed the lead to 21-12.

Bell added another touchdown later in the quarter, this one on a 7-yard toss play, and Cache Hammond's 37-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter made it 30-12.

That was 30 straight points for Grantsville.

San Juan finally showed some life again late in the fourth when Yeomans found Palmer for a 39-yard touchdown with 5:25 remaining and Randall Black ran in the two-point conversion to make it 30-20.

The Broncos got one more chance when they forced Grantsville to punt, but after driving deep into Cowboys territory, Yeomans threw another interception to Graeson Warren.

That was Warren's second interception of the night and effectively ended San Juan's final serious threat.

For Millward, the biggest thing wasn't that his team played a perfect game. It absolutely didn't. It was that the Cowboys kept fighting anyway.

"I'm just so proud of our kids," Millward said. "They just battled and battled, and we made a lot of mistakes, but they just kept believing."

Grantsville's defense did more than just create turnovers. It swarmed San Juan throughout the night.

"They just swarm and swarm," Millward said. "That's what we like to say, that we just play hard-nosed football in Grantsville, and I feel like tonight, that's what we did."

And that's probably the best way to describe the game. San Juan looked like the better team early, then Grantsville made play after play.

For a Grantsville team that spent much of the first half leaving points on the field, its defense made sure it would get enough chances to eventually make them count.

And when the Cowboys finally did, they didn't stop.

title: Good Sports: Fresno dad turns hobby into unforgettable moment with Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott
description: A Fresno father's custom tribute hat for Dak Prescott turned a year-old painting hobby into an unforgettable, full-circle moment.
fullText:
A Fresno father's painting hobby led to an unforgettable encounter when Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott not only accepted one of his custom hats, but later wore it and sought out the artist behind it.

Mario Corona, a stay-at-home dad, licensed EMT and aspiring firefighter, began painting hats about a year ago. He said he never expected one of his designs would end up in the hands of an NFL quarterback.

"A day that I definitely won't forget," Corona said.

Recently, Corona completed a Dallas Cowboys collection that included a tribute to Prescott's brother, Jace. Prescott lost his brother to suicide in 2020 and has spoken publicly about raising awareness since then.

Corona created what he calls an "Angel Hat," featuring a portrait of Jace on the side.

"I know as a Cowboys fan, as a Dak fan, I know how much his brother meant to him and his motivation," Corona said.

Corona traveled to Cowboys training camp in Oxnard hoping to personally give the hat to Prescott. During First Responders Appreciation Day, he was able to get on the field.

"The players right in front of Dak were CeeDee [Lamb] and [George] Pickens, which were the players that were on my hat that I was wearing at the time. So I got caught up in trying to show them the hat I was wearing," Corona said. "By the time they passed and I turned back, Dak was already right here. I just babbled out whatever words were trying to come out of my mouth. Luckily, he did grab it before walking off."

Prescott accepted the hat without initially noticing the portrait painted on its side.

"I was happy that I knew he took it at least. I was actually leaving training camp pretty bummed. I didn't sell any hats, I didn't get any autographs," Corona said.

After leaving camp, Corona saw photos on social media showing Prescott wearing the hat. That is when he learned the quarterback was looking for the artist who created it.

"Got in the car, drove back... they're like, dude, you're going to have to go to the hotel," Corona said.

Corona later reunited with Prescott and captured the interaction on his Meta glasses.

"It was just real. It felt real," Corona said. "You know that moment was bigger than an autograph."

Throughout the remainder of training camp, Prescott was seen wearing Corona's hat.

The positive response to his work has encouraged Corona to take the next step with his business. He said he plans to open for commissions in November.

"As long as you're passionate about it and you stay dedicated... progress will come. If you're trying, you're going to have improvement. It for sure has paid off," Corona said.

title: Stolen Super Bowl ring has Bernie Kosar asking Jerry Jones for a replacement
description: Bernie Kosar asked Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones for a replacement after his original Super Bowl ring was stolen.
fullText:
Stolen Super Bowl ring has Bernie Kosar asking Jerry Jones for a replacement originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Bernie Kosar is still remembered well by fans of the Cleveland Browns. He guided the franchise to three AFC Championship games during the late 1980s, and is considered one of their best quarterbacks ever.

He later went to the Dallas Cowboys, where he played as a backup quarterback. He managed to win Super Bowl XXVIII in the 1993 season, the only time he won it in his career. Kosar is now asking his former franchise's owner for help after a horrible incident.

Kosar was drafted by the Browns in 1985 and spent eight seasons with them as the starting quarterback. After being released in 1993, he joined the Cowboys as the backup to Troy Aikman for one season. Though he only played for four games, that was the only season he managed to win the Lombardi Trophy, a career high for him.

He did play an important role in the NFC Championship game against the San Francisco 49ers, after Aikman was unavailable in the second half of the game due to a concussion. He was also heavily involved during Super Bowl week, helping to prepare the team with offensive coordinator Norv Turner and even appeared in the final play of the Super Bowl game against the Buffalo Bills.

Kosar recently appeared on the August 12, 2026, episode of The Sage Steele Show. He revealed that the Super Bowl XXVIII championship ring he earned with the Cowboys was stolen. He asked for Cowboys owner Jerry Jones to get a replacement ring for the one he lost.

He said, "I lost it, so I can't wear it. And Jerry, I'm going to be calling you because it got stolen. I'm going to be calling you for another one, bro. So, please help me out again."

So far, Jones has not yet responded to this plea for help. Details about the theft are still unknown, and it remains to be seen if the Cowboys owner can manage another Super Bowl ring for him. Kosar recently got compared to one current player of the Browns.

Browns legend Hanford Dixon recently compared franchise quarterback Shedeur Sanders with Kosar. Kosar and Dixon were teammates, and the comparison was praiseworthy for Sanders. Speaking on the BIGPLAY Cleveland Show, he said, "I see Bernie Kosar. And what I mean by that is, one thing we knew about Bernie, is that Bernie was very confident. I mean, he was a guy that believed in his ability, he knew that he could play, and knew that he could play quarterback."

He added, "Shedeur is the same way. He's a very confident guy. Some people call him cocky. I don't have a problem with him being cocky. But I think this guy is very, very confident. He knows that he can play, he believes that he can play. He's the type of guy at the quarterback position that a team rallies themselves around him. They'll get behind this guy if we give him the chance to prove himself."

Bernie Kosar will be hoping that Sanders manages to emulate him, and that the Cowboys get him a replacement ring.

Jerry Jones turns $140 million investment into mind-blowing $15.5 billion Cowboys empire originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Dallas Cowboys continue dominating global sports financial rankings without showing any signs of slowing down. Team owner Jerry Jones purchased the franchise back in 1989 for merely $140 million. That initial investment yielded unprecedented financial growth over three decades.

Sportico recently valued the legendary franchise at a staggering $15.5 billion. This massive number represents a 21% jump from their previous 2025 valuation. Jones built a true financial juggernaut despite missing the playoffs frequently over recent years.

ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter shared a massive valuation update across social media platforms Tuesday morning. Schefter quoted a Sportico article ranking historic franchises above every global sports organization worldwide. This marks the seventh straight year Cowboys secured top spot globally.

"Sportico once again named the Dallas Cowboys as the most valuable franchise in sports," Schefter wrote. "Listing their value at $15.5 billion. Jerry Jones' franchise has been the most valuable in sports in every iteration of Sportico's valuations."

The franchise currently sits $2.8 billion ahead of the second place Los Angeles Rams. New York Giants rank third overall valued at $12 billion. The New England Patriots round out the top five alongside the New York Jets.

The merchandise business generates nearly $200 million annually for the Dallas organization. The team secured massive $300 million in annual sponsorship revenue doubling every other franchise. Global brand recognition remains completely unmatched across the entire league.

Dallas only managed four playoff victories since 2000 despite immense financial success. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer enters second season leading a talented roster forward. Jones firmly believes the current coaching staff can guide the team toward championship soon.

"I like what we've got in our coaching staff," Jones said. "I like what we've got in the makeup of our players; I think we're extraordinarily sound in the way we're approaching all sides of the ball… I think we can be a contender."

Quarterback Dak Prescott leads an explosive offense alongside CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Offense ranked second overall averaging 391.9 yards per game. Defense ranked worst allowing 30.1 points per game last season. The organization desperately needs defensive improvement to match elite offensive production. The front office remains confident this group can finally break through.

title: Can Cowboys remain among Top 5 in this key offensive tactic in 2026?
description: The Dallas Cowboys ranked in the NFL's top 5 in yards/RPO last year and there's plenty of reason to lean into that in 2026.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys are always looking for ways to make their offense better and their overall attack more bulletproof. Winning a variety of different ways is key to sustained success in the postseason, so it's been a focus of Klayton Adams as he enters Year 2 as Dallas' offensive coordinator.

Designing and executing a scoring drive in the modern-day NFL is no easy task. With defenses shifting to more umbrella looks in the secondary, big plays can be hard to come by, even for a star-studded team like the Cowboys. Oftentimes the only way to put up points is to put together long, multi-play drives. In drives such as these, unsuccessful plays can have disastrous consequences. It's why many coordinators speak incessantly about "staying ahead of the chains."

The Cowboys used a myriad of techniques to do so, but one that worked to great effect in 2025 and probably even moreso in 2026 is that of the run-pass option.

Staying ahead of the chains means focusing more on success rate than expected points added (today's primary metrics for grading value), which means low-risk/low-reward plays are often preferable to those high-risk/high-reward plays often associated with big shots downfield.

The Cowboys aren't particularly dedicated to any single identity. One moment they will show the patience demanded for sustained and conservative drives, the next moment they're launching missiles downfield looking for homeruns.  While everyone knows a Cowboys offense with Dak Prescott, Ceedee Lamb and George Pickens is proficient in big plays, they're also strong in building multi-play drives.

While the league average for plays per drive was 5.6 last season, the Cowboys were league leaders at 6.5 plays per drive. It might not sound like much but for a well-rounded and fairly aggressive team such as Dallas, being a leader in plays per drive is impressive. One of the ways they achieved this impressive accomplishment is by being proficient in RPOs.

Dak Prescott RPO work, quick screen to CeeDee Lamb pic.twitter.com/94v9BBAzaz

Based on Pro Football Focus play tracking, the Cowboys were fourth in the NFL in yards per play on RPOs last season. At 5.5 yards/RPO, the Cowboys were a full yard above league average. It kept them ahead of the chains and kept defenses on their heels.

RPOs are effective because they put defenders in conflict. Not to be confused with read-option and zone-read which are run-only option plays, RPOs have a legit pass option to their design.

In a nutshell, if a defender plays it one way, the quarterback hands it off. If the defender plays it another way, the quarterback pulls it back and delivers a pass. It's a quick-read play that requires quick decisions. It's low-risk and low-reward but has a success rate of 52.3% compared to that of non-RPO plays which average 48.1%.

An added benefit of an RPO-rich offense is the stress it removes from offensive tackles. With such a quick-strike nature, RPOs get the ball out quickly. Per PFF, Patrick Mahomes, king of the RPO, averaged 1.17 seconds on RPO throws. It's a great way to neutralize a defense that has elite edge rushers.

RPOs also typically favor inside runs. With arguably the best inside offensive line in the NFL, the Cowboys have reason to run plays up the middle. And since most RPOs end up being runs, it plays perfectly to Dallas' strength. With one of the great field generals in the game in Prescott, the Cowboys should by no means become an RPO-rich offense in 2026 but given their proficiency in it, and given their pass protection situation on the edge, a slight uptick might be in order.

It's all about becoming multidimensional and being bulletproof for the postseason. Explosive plays aren't always an option but RPOs have a certain resiliency that ages well in an NFL season. Last seen, the Cowboys were pretty darn good at them, so why not lean into RPOs a little more in 2026 and see if it pays off like the data suggests?

title: Seahawks prep for Saturday Football Fest
description: We’re a little more than a week away from the Seahawks’ preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys. Thursday, the team had to take practice inside because of the smoke. Saturday, they will pack Lumen Field for the “Seahawks’ Football Fest”.
fullText:
We're a little more than a week away from the Seahawks' preseason opener against the Dallas Cowboys.

Thursday, the team had to take practice inside because of the smoke. Saturday, they will pack Lumen Field for the "Seahawks' Football Fest".

The event is an evening of football, family, and fun. Featuring meet-and-greets, photo-ops with franchise legends, a live DJ, and team mascots.

Rashid Shaheed is going through his first training camp with the Hawks after joining the team midseason last year.

"I'm excited to see the energy of the fans," said the wide receiver. "It's going to be good to get back on home turf. And it's going to be a ton of good energy. We're all excited."

Tickets are still available, and they're about $17 each. A family-friendly way to enjoy the Seahawks up close before the season kicks off.

Gates open around 4:15 pm, and practice starts at 5:20 pm.

Plus, there'll be an autographed football toss around 7:20 pm.

However, while some of the younger players couldn't wait to get back in front of the 12's, one veteran admitted he was contemplating retirement this past offseason.

Linebacker Demarcus Lawrence said last year if the Hawks won it all, he'd hang up his cleats.

But, after a Super Bowl ring, as well as a discussion with his wife, he's said he's back for a 13th season. Eager to defend the championship he'd been chasing his whole career.

"With the type of team that we have…we should've been where we were last year," the veteran Linebacker calmly asserts.

"This is where the hard part begins, staying on top."

Lawrence admits winning the Lombardi Trophy was bittersweet. He says he couldn't walk away. He compared the situation to going from being the hunter chasing a goal to the hunted defending a title.

"They say it's no fun when the rabbit has the gun," Lawrence smirked.

"We're the ones with the dot on our back. So, I just want to see how that feels."

After spending his entire career with Dallas, Lawrence joined the Seahawks last offseason. He says the brotherhood on defense, especially with so many journeymen, is genuine.

"It's just great to have those caliber of leaders in the locker room with you. Like-minded guys."

That culture is on full display this year, thanks in part to HBO's Hard Knocks.

The training camp docuseries debuted earlier this week. And, Shaheed said everyone's hoping for a starring role.

"A ton of laughs, a ton of jokes. It's kind of cool to see how HBO portrays our team on TV," Shaheed said.

He says it's been a great insight into the mindset inside the building. A look at how the team competes against each other and how the franchise operates from top to bottom.

"I'm excited to continue to watch," says Shaheed.

title: Dallas Cowboys Sign Former Giants Running Back
description: The Dallas Cowboys have signed former New York Giants running back and 2025 UFL rushing leader Jashaun Corbin. The post Dallas Cowboys Sign Former Giants Running Back appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys are bringing in another running back for training camp in hopes of creating much-needed depth that was missing in 2025.

"Dallas Cowboys signing running back Jashaun Corbin, per a league source," NFL reporter Aaron Wilson wrote on his official X account on Friday.

"The Dallas Cowboys have signed Orlando Storm RB Jashaun Corbin," UFL/NFL reporter James Larsen wrote on his official X account on Friday. "Corbin had a strong campaign with Orlando this past UFL season, rushing for 463 yards & 3 TD's. Led UFL in rushing yards in 2025 w/ Brahmas. Another well deserved opportunity for Jashaun."

"The Cowboys have signed RB Jashaun Corbin and waived RB Dominic Richardson," The Athletic's Jon Machota wrote on his official X account on Friday.

Corbin, 5-foot-11 and 224 pounds, spent 2 seasons at Texas A&M and 2 seasons at Florida State before going undrafted in 2022. He played 2 seasons for the Giants in 2022 and 2023 and has also spent time with the Carolina Panthers, Atlanta Falcons, and New England Patriots.

His UFL career has included playing for the San Antonio Brahmas in 2025 and the Orlando Storm in 2026.

"Corbin has decent size and good vision, but he will need to play with better decisiveness early in the rep, as his play speed and cut quickness are unlikely to aid him enough in eluding NFL tacklers," NFL draft analyst Lance Zierlein wrote in his 2022 pre-draft evaluation. "He responds fairly well to block development and runs with some pop, but it's hard to find an area of his game that really stands out."

The Cowboys made a big move at running back this offseason by signing free agent Javonte Williams to a 3-year, $24 million contract after he rushed for 1,200 yards playing for Dallas on a 1-year, $3 million "prove it" contract in 2025.

One place the Cowboys did not find any luck at the running back position was in the NFL Draft, where they selected 2 running backs in 2025, with Jaydon Blue (5th round) and Phil Mafah (7th round).

That duo combined for a whopping 147 yards and 2 touchdowns as rookies, and both appear on the road to being out-and-out busts.

title: Packers’ Micah Parsons eyeing Week 6 vs. Cowboys for return from ACL tear
description: Packers star Micah Parsons is hoping to be back from his ACL tear by Week 6 against his old team, the Cowboys.
fullText:
Packers' Micah Parsons eyeing Week 6 vs. Cowboys for return from ACL tear appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The Green Bay Packers are hoping to contend for an NFC Championship again this season, as they have one of the best rosters in the NFC coming into the season. However, they are still working on getting all of their stars healthy from an injury-riddled 2025 season before Week 1.

Unfortunately, it looks like Micah Parsons' knee injury is going to linger into the season. The star pass rusher tore his ACL in a game against the Denver Broncos late in the season and missed the remainder of the year. He has spent the entire offseason rehabbing, but is currently on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list during training camp and is expected to be sidelined for Week 1 and beyond.

Now, Parsons has revealed a potential target date for his return. The Packers play against his old team, the Dallas Cowboys, in Week 6 on Oct. 18, and Parsons says it is a possibility he will be back for that game, per Ryan Wood of USA Today.

"Is it possible? Yes, so I wouldn't say it's not possible," Parsons said. "At the same time, in the next 10, 12 weeks from now, we've got to make it possible by putting the work in."

It's not ideal that the Packers will have to play any games without Parsons on the field, but thankfully it sounds like he should be back by midseason. The former Penn State star transformed the Packers' defense last season after Green Bay acquired him in a trade with the Cowboys. If they want to make a push for a Super Bowl this season, they need him back at 100%.

Thankfully for the Packers, star tight end Tucker Kraft is already back on the field after recovering from his torn ACL. Kraft was seen biking out to training camp last week and has been taken off of the PUP list. Kraft suffered his injury earlier last season, so it's a good sign to see him already back on the field.

If the Packers want to make a run this year, they will need both Parsons and Kraft to be back at their best.

title: Cowboys suffer first season-ending injury, TE out for year with ACL
description: The Cowboys suffered their first casualty of camp as tight end Princeton Fant suffered a torn ACL on the first day of padded practice.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys first padded practice came at a cost as reserve tight end Princeton Fant has suffered a season-ending knee injury. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer confirmed an initially feared diagnosis that the fourth-year tight end tore his ACL and partially tore his MCL.

He will have surgery at a later date, but the fourth-year veteran's road ahead is now centered on an extensive rehabilitation process and recovery, putting his immediate future on hold.

Per Brian Schottenheimer, TE Princeton Fant suffered an ACL, partial MCL injury. He'll undergo surgery in a few weeks. #dallascowboys

Initial reports confirmed Fant would undergo further testing, including an MRI, to determine the severity of the injury.

Fant was engaged in a blocking rep on a running play against edge Sam Williams when he suffered the injury, immediately falling onto the ground. He remained down for several moments before being helped to the sideline and eventually carted off, unable to put weight on his left leg.

Princeton Fant left on a cart after this collision: pic.twitter.com/f5ZkkFTWyn

Fant entered the league as a 2023 undrafted free agent out of Tennessee and has spent the last three seasons in Dallas working towards a permanent roster spot. He had appeared in 11 career games but has yet to catch a regular season pass.

Dallas maintains depth at tight end with Jake Ferguson and Brevyn Spann-Ford headlining. Fant was in competition with Luke Schoonmaker along with UDFAs Michael Trigg and DJ Rogers. Fant's absence thins the unit's overall versatility.

Repetitions that would have gone to Fant will now have to be redistributed, potentially accelerating the developmental timeline for others. Fant will move to the IR list, opening up a roster spot for a new addition who will try and make his mark and impress the coaching staff.

title: Tyler Guyton will remain with the Cowboys' first-team at LT
description: The Cowboys went into their offseason program with a competition between Tyler Guyton and Nate Thomas for the left tackle job.
fullText:
The Cowboys went into their offseason program with a competition between Tyler Guyton and Nate Thomas for the left tackle job. The job appears about decided after one padded practice in training camp.

Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said at his news conference Tuesday that the competition isn't over, but Guyton is the clear leader. Thomas had been scheduled to take first-team reps in practice Tuesday.

The Cowboys started camp with the left tackle spot as the only question on offense from last season with every starter returning, and Guyton was expected to win the job.

The Cowboys drafted Guyton with the 29th overall pick in 2024, 204 picks before selecting Thomas. Guyton, though, has struggled with inconsistency and injuries.

He has missed nine games in two seasons.

In 2025, Guyton's knee injury in training camp gave Thomas reps with the first-team offense in practice. Thomas ended up making his first four career starts in 2025, but Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith started the final four games at left tackle when Guyton was out with a high-ankle sprain.

Guyton played primarily right tackle at the University of Oklahoma.

title: Cowboys Waive 6-foot-6, 250-Pound Edge Rusher Facing 3-Game Suspension
description: The Dallas Cowboys have waived free-agent edge rusher Charles Snowden, who is facing a 3-game suspension from the NFL. The post Cowboys Waive 6-foot-6, 250-Pound Edge Rusher Facing 3-Game Suspension appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Dallas Cowboys were willing to take a chance on edge rusher Charles Snowden — they just weren’t willing to wait for him to heal up as they try to improve the NFL’s worst defense from 1 season ago.

“The Cowboys have signed OL Sebastian Gutierrez and waived OLB Charles Snowden,” The Athletic’s Jon Machota wrote on his official X account on Sunday.

Snowden signed a 1-year, $1.075 million contract with the Cowboys on June 18 and was suspended almost 1 month later. Snowden was waived with an injury designation as he was dealing with a groin issue.

“Cowboys DE Charles Snowden has been suspended for the first three games of the season, per today’s wire,” ESPN’s Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on July 14. “Snowden, per the NFL, ‘is eligible to participate in all preseason activities, including games; his suspension will take effect as of the roster reduction to 53 players.”

He was arrested for a DUI in Las Vegas in December 2024 and pleaded no contest in January 2026.

“Cowboys DE Charles Snowden has been suspended for the first three games of the season because of a DUI,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport wrote on his official X account on July 14. “The news of his personal conduct violation was on today’s wire.”

Snowden would have been eligible to return to the Cowboys for a Week 4 home game against the Arizona Cardinals.

Snowden, 6-foot-6 and 250 pounds, started 9 games each of the last 2 seasons for the Las Vegas Raiders, with 67 tackles, 4.5 sacks, 8 TFL, and 11 QB hits in that stretch.

NFL draft analyst Lance Zierlein projected Snowden as a 4th-round pick in 2021.

“Versatile defender who has worked both open and closed sides as an even-front edge defender,” Zierlein wrote. “Snowden is a long, smooth athlete dropping into space or transitioning with change of direction. Lower-body anchor is an issue and he needs more play strength, but he’s usually first to land his hands and does an adequate job of separating and setting the edge. Despite having some twitch with his get-off as a rusher, he gets locked out of the cookie jar due to an inability to convert at the top of the rush with hand usage or go-to counters. However, he has excellent lateral quickness for use in twists and stunts and has surprising potential as a zone or man defender when asked. Snowden is an ascending prospect with Day 2 potential as a 3-4 outside linebacker, but his ceiling will be defined by whether he can add mass and improve his rush.”

fullText:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — CBS NFL analyst and former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo had an open container of alcohol in his vehicle when he was stopped by police last week and later arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence, authorities said.

According to one of three citations released by the Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office, the “open bottle of an alcoholic beverage” was discovered in the passenger’s side of Romo’s black Jeep during an inventory before it was towed.

Another citation said police stopped Romo on Interstate 43 on July 23 after he was seen passing cars in a gore area, which separates interstate traffic from cars entering from an on-ramp. Police said Romo questioned what a gore area was during the stop.

Romo performed poorly on field sobriety tests and was taken into custody, booked and released. Court records show Romo was later cited for refusing “to take test for intoxication after arrest.” He has a court appearance scheduled for Sept. 21.

According to body camera footage released earlier this week, Romo told deputies he had been coming from a golf course and was on his way “to visit grandma and grandpa” when he was stopped.

A deputy told Romo he suspected him of being impaired because he had “red glassy eyes” and an “odor of an intoxicating alcoholic beverage.”

Romo went to high school about 35 miles from Milwaukee in Burlington, Wisconsin.

The 46-year-old Romo has been the lead game analyst for CBS’ NFL coverage since 2017 after making four Pro Bowl appearances during an NFL career that ran from 2004-16 and was spent entirely with Dallas.

Romo remains the Cowboys’ franchise leader in career touchdown passes with 248. He held the franchise record for career passing yards (34,183) until Dak Prescott overtook him last season.

title: Jerry Jones opens Dallas Cowboys training camp with drama, willing to make trade to bolster Super Bowl chances
description: Leave it to owner Jerry Jones to add a little spark to what had been a largely quiet offseason for the Dallas Cowboys, even while admitting he planned to do...
fullText:
Leave it to owner Jerry Jones to add a little spark to what had been a largely quiet offseason for the Dallas Cowboys, even while admitting he planned to do no such thing.

Jones simply can’t help himself.

Of course, things started normally at the press conference on Tuesday to open Cowboys training camp for the 2026 season in Oxnard, Calif..

Jones initially, made fun of the idea that the Cowboys had a quiet offseason, considering all the moves they made with the coaching staff, hiring nine new assistants, led by defensive coordinator Christian Parker.

And Jones, who admitted last year that when things are quiet around the Cowboys he would often do something to stir the pot, played along with the perception.

“I’ve never thought that there was anything quiet or subdued about the Dallas Cowboys,” Jones said. “I’ve never thought of it that way, but I have been guilty of stirring it up. And you guys help me. And we have been a great team. I promise you that for the last 30 something years. And so that does happen and it is good. I do like the perception that we’ve had a quiet uneventful off season and let’s see how we can work in that. Perception is big. Perception is big. But what I will tell you is I don’t plan on doing anything around here for the next few days to stir anything up.”

It certainly helped that there was no contract drama with receiver George Pickens, who signed his franchise tag and joined the team for camp with no plans of a hold out.

“I personally like the fact that the perception is that it’s been a quiet, non-confrontational off season,” Jones said. “That’s good. I have really a lot of that where I live in my mind. I do, but I have some times when it’s not fun too. So all that’s good. I like the mood.”

And yet, a few minutes later when asked about Super Bowl chances, Jones bolstered quarterback Dak Prescott’s Super Bowl or bust mantra for 2026 by adding his own drama to proceedings with a promise to add a difference-making player to make it happen.

He said he feels that good about his team and their hopes of ending what is now a 31-year drought since their last Super Bowl title following the 1995 season.

“I’d give up future to add substantive to where we are today as to a player, to give you an idea about would I invest something substantive to get the right kind of deal to improve us opening day. I would,” Jones said. “I feel that good about this team this year.”

Jones then doubled down on his comments by saying he talked to a owner on Monday about making a “substantive” trade.

“I think we’ve got a chance to be worthy of spending some future if we saw an opportunity,” Jones said. “Those kinds of conversations that are ongoing…I talked about a situation yesterday with another team and another owner. Yesterday.”

Jones comments only opened the door to widespread speculation on which owner he talked to and which player he was talking about.

It also spawned a question about the failed trade attempt for Las Vegas Raiders defensive Maxx Crosby in March and whether it could be back in play.

Crosby was initially dealt to the Baltimore Ravens, who then backed out the deal because of injury concerns.

Jones still acknowledges that one of the key areas they could bolster a difference-making player is edge rusher/defensive end.

Why did you walk away from Max Crosby when it fell apart with the Ravens and not revisit that then?

Can you elaborate on that for me?

“No, because there’s nothing more to elaborate about, but we did not walk away,” Jones said. “That’s about all there is to say, but we understood his injury well. And so we thought he could help us then. And we’re surprised the way that was resolved. But to basically take what happened with him after he came home back to the Raiders, to inject anything about what we’re thinking or doing and because he went back to the Raiders would be a mistake.”

Vice president Stephen Jones had to chime in and let Jerry Jones know that because Crosby is still with the Raiders he is getting close to tampering by continuing the conversation.

When asked in general of Crosby was the type of difference-making player he was looking to add, Jones responded in kind.

“Let’s don’t hypothetical here…That is tampering,” Jones said. “It really is. And so we don’t want to talk like that and act like that. But that is a good example of what you can stand ready for if in fact you think the rest of your team is coming along well, then those things stay alive. It is a good indicator of how good we feel about the team, the fact that we could do things like you’re talking about right there. I’ve really got to emphasize here he is a Raider. He’s a complete Raider, a happy Raider, everything in the book. And we shouldn’t even be having this kind of discussion with him.”

Now regarding the discussions with the other owner, there is nothing imminent on the horizon, Jones said No trade is afoot for the Cowboys.

But he is ready and willing to do something to light a fire under the Cowboys’ Super Bowl chances after what has been a “quiet” offseason.

Prescott has said as much and embodied the team’s goal by arriving to training camp with Super Bowl t-shirt on.

“That’s always been my mindset. It’s the one thing I truly love about the Cowboys organization and the fanbase is it’s that or nothing,” Prescott said recently. “As I said wherever that was, that’s what being a competitor is. If that’s not how you’re wired, if that’s not how you think, whether you’re a fan, whether you’re a player, whether you’re a coach, then I think you’re in the wrong business and honestly I don’t want you on my team. I love those expectations and they’ll always be there.”

“Dak’s feeling about it is more important than me feeling about it because Dak actually tangibly can cause his teammates to play at a higher level than I can,” Jones said. “So when Dak is that positive about it, that adds some credibility to it. I too can say that the fact that Dak is looking at what he’s looking at causes me to feel the same way. I think we’ve got a chance to really be good. I love the excitement.”

“You guys don’t expect us to be a contender in the Super Bowl,” Jones added while pointing to the media. Y’all don’t? Why would you? I like that. I do. I like that. And I like what we put together to show you that we can do it.”

He also plans to add to it, if necessary to make it happen.

Just don’t ask about Maxx Crosby.

title: Linebacker Dante Fowler Jr. eager to make impact on Seahawks talented defense
description: For veteran linebacker Dante Fowler, Jr., the chance to join the Seattle Seahawks wasn't something he was going to pass up again. fullText:
SEATTLE (AP) — For veteran linebacker Dante Fowler, Jr., the chance to join the Seattle Seahawks wasn't something he was going to pass up again.

After finishing with three sacks and 15 total tackles with Dallas last season, Fowler signed a one-year contract with the Seahawks in May worth up to $5 million.

Fowler, the No. 3 overall draft pick by the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2015, considered signing in Seattle last year before opting to go back to the Cowboys. But after an aggressive sales pitch from Seahawks veteran and former Cowboys teammate DeMarcus Lawrence, along with a visit to the team headquarters, he knew the time was finally right.

“You can see why they won the Super Bowl, whether it's on or off the field,” Fowler said. “It’s actually pretty cool to see the camaraderie here from the top to the bottom, front office and the team. It’s a great group of guys. You come into this building happy, and you come in looking forward to going to work.”

Fowler is stepping into an enviable situation for a free agent signee, with the Seahawks returning the majority of last year’s dominant defense. Linebacker Boye Mafe (Cincinnati), safety Coby Bryant (Chicago), and cornerback Riq Woolen (Philadelphia) were the most notable losses, but the Seahawks are expected to once again be among the league's best.

Even on a defense as heralded as Seattle, a veteran presence like Fowler can still help make everyone better.

“The way he comes in, he works. I think from a football aspect, like what he’s going to bring to that room, pass rush-wise, Lord, like, he’s able to get off the rock,” linebacker Ernest Jones IV said. “He has so many moves in his bag, and it’s only going to make the guys around him better.”

Fowler was also attracted to Seattle by the presence of defensive coordinator Aden Durde, who Fowler first worked with in Atlanta in 2020 when Durde was a defensive assistant, then in Dallas when Durde coached the Cowboys’ defensive line.

Durde tried hard to recruit Fowler to Seattle last season, and Fowler is excited to once again be working with the Seahawks British-born coach.

“Just to see the way he’s grown throughout his career, and being my defensive line coach at the Cowboys to now his role as a defensive coordinator here, is very awesome,” Fowler said.

Along with Durde, Fowler is eager to continue working with Seattle’s strength and conditioning staff, which he says is the best he’s ever worked with.

Fowler credits the staff for getting him into fantastic shape, which gives him optimism that he’ll have a big year like in 2024, when he had 10 1/2 sacks and 39 tackles with Washington.

“I feel like how it felt when I played in Washington with the Commanders,” Fowler said. “I just knew I was going to have a great season just because of the work that I put in all season, and how good of a shape I was. So I feel like that.”

Head coach Mike Macdonald has already started to feel Fowler’s impact three days into training camp.

“You want to affect the quarterback, but not too much at this point," Macdonald said, “so he’s doing great. He’s getting used to how we roll here, and I think he’s enjoying his time, which is positive. Definitely seeing flashes for sure.”

While he wasn’t a member of last year’s Super Bowl-winning squad, Fowler hasn’t struggled to fit in on a Seahawks team that already has plenty of star talent on defense.

“I just fall in line and do what I’m supposed to do,” Fowler said. “They already had a great defense before we got here, and they won a Super Bowl. It was the best defense in the world last year. So my job is to just fall in line and do whatever I’ve got to do to make this defense upgrade a little bit more.”
